AVS is a paid B2B service that helps strategically grow complex brands on Amazon. As an Account Manager (internally referred to as Senior Brand Specialist), you will own and drive the strategic relationship with a portfolio of complex vendor accounts operating across multiple EU marketplaces. You will navigate the unique dynamics of each market while building unified, customer-centric business plans that create value for both end customers and your vendor partners. You will own your vendors' annual Vendor Growth Plans (VGPs) and be a key contributor to Joint Business Planning (JBP), shaping the 3-year strategic direction alongside your vendors. You will translate performance insights into strategic priorities across four key areas: selection and product lifecycle management, supply-chain and operational excellence, marketing and brand visibility, and commercial performance optimization. You will leverage advanced data analytics and generative AI tools to identify growth opportunities, inform business planning, and develop solutions that balance vendor goals with customer experience. In a fast-evolving environment where data, tools, and customer expectations change rapidly, you will be expected to move with speed, embrace new technologies, and find creative solutions that require novel approaches not yet tested before. . Working cross-functionally with partner teams across Category Management, Supply Chain, Finance, and Marketing, you will lead initiatives that drive sustainable, long-term growth.

Key job responsibilities
- Commercial Performance & Strategic Planning: Own and drive the growth strategy for a portfolio of complex Pan-EU vendor accounts. Develop and own strategic, customer-centric Vendor Growth Plans (VGPs) and contribute to Joint Business Planning (JBP), using data-driven insights to set priorities and create solutions for both end customers and vendor partners

- Availability & Operational Excellence: Lead Pan-EU supply-chain strategy, driving cost reduction, defect elimination, and operational improvements at scale across your portfolio

- Marketing & Brand Visibility: Define and execute marketing strategies that drive traffic, conversion, and brand growth. Partner with Amazon Advertising and vendor teams to deliver measurable customer and business impact

- Selection & Product Lifecycle: Drive strategic selection expansion and product lifecycle management. Identify market gaps, lead new product launches, and ensure the end-customer experience meets the highest bar

- Cross-functional Leadership: Lead cross-functional initiatives, collaborate with internal teams (Category Management, Supply Chain, Finance, Marketing), and translate insights into actionable recommendations that inform both short-term actions and long-term planning

- People Development: Act as a mentor and coach to junior team members, supporting their growth and development within the team

target_jobs.description:
Reverse Logistics Services (RLS) exists to make returns effortless and reliable for every Amazon customer — no matter which store or partner they walk into. In Italy, we deliver that experience across more than 17,000 partner and carrier locations, through convenience-led options such as Label-Free, Box-Free (LFBF) drop-off and every other way a customer can return an item in-store.
The ISX Regional Partner Coach, Italy owns the quality and consistency of that experience across the whole Italian network. Because returns run through thousands of independent partner sites, the experience can vary widely from one location to the next and the core of this role is closing that gap. You will get into the field, see how returns actually happen at partner locations, coach partners and their teams to the standard customers expect, and use data to focus your time on the sites that need help most. Your mission is holistic: improving in-store returns execution across all return types, so a customer's experience is just as good at the busiest location as it is at the smallest.
This is not only a field-execution role. It carries a strategic remit that reflects its level. Beyond coaching individual sites, you will help design and deploy the network-wide improvements that lift the entire Italian network at once: in-store signage and wayfinding, store supplies and replenishment mechanisms, associate support and training, and the tools partners rely on to process returns. You will translate what you learn in the field into scalable programs, work across internal teams to launch them in Italy, and help shape how the broader EU standards themselves are built, turning local, on-the-ground insight into lasting structural improvement.
This is also a founding, build-from-scratch role. You'll be the first ISX Partner Coach in Italy and one of the earliest members of the EU field team, reporting directly to the EU ISX Senior Manager. There's no established playbook yet, you'll help create it. We're looking for someone with real ambition, comfort with ambiguity, and the judgment to focus relentlessly on the initiatives that matter most while the team, tools, and standards are still taking shape.

Key job responsibilities
• Own the in-store returns experience in Italy across ~17,000 partner and carrier locations, ensuring returns are fast, easy, and reliable for customers across all return types.
• Get into the field and coach. Visit partner locations, observe how returns are handled, and coach partner teams to Amazon's standards for speed, accuracy, and customer experience.
• Use data to prioritize. You can't be everywhere. Use performance data to identify the locations and partners falling furthest behind and concentrate your effort where it improves the customer experience most.
• Drive measurable improvement on the metrics that define a great returns experience: how fast customers are served, how reliably returns are processed, customer satisfaction, and site readiness.
• Deploy network-wide improvements. Lead the rollout of scalable programs that raise the standard across the entire Italian network, including in-store signage and wayfinding, store supplies and replenishment, associate support and training, and returns-processing tools , using your field insight to prioritize and adapt them for the market.
• Shape strategy from the field. Turn on-the-ground observations into recommendations that influence how EU-wide returns standards, mechanisms, and programs are designed, ensuring the field perspective is built in from the start.
• Manage performance to resolution. Follow a structured coaching and follow-up cycle for underperforming sites, and partner with the right internal teams (Business Partnerships for retail partners, the Transportation team for carriers) when issues need to be escalated to a partner's leadership.
• Build the foundation. As a founding team member, help shape how the EU field team audits, coaches, and reports, adapting proven practices from the North America team to the Italian market and feed your field insights into the monthly ISX reporting that informs strategy.


A day in the life
You start the week by reviewing performance data for Italy and identifying the partner locations and carriers falling furthest behind on the customer experience. You spend time in the field visiting a risk-weighted set of those sites, watching real customers complete returns, checking that the process is running smoothly, and coaching partner teams on the spot. Back at your desk, you're also driving the Italy rollout of a new signage standard and a store-supplies replenishment mechanism, using what you saw in the field to shape how they're deployed. You log your findings, build improvement plans for the sites that need them, escalate the bigger systemic issues to the right internal team, and close the week by capturing insights for the monthly ISX report and re-planning around wherever the customer experience needs you most.

About the team
Reverse Logistics Services (RLS) owns the returns journey end-to-end for Amazon, everything that happens after a customer decides to send something back until delivery at our FC. Our purpose is simple but hard: make returns effortless and reliable for every customer, while running one of the largest, most complex reverse-logistics networks in retail.

Within RLS, the In-Store Experience (ISX) team focuses on where returns meet the real world, the thousands of partner and carrier locations customers walk into to drop off an item. We turn a single promise into a consistent reality across every one of them: fast, easy, dependable returns, no matter which door a customer chooses. Working from the field, we close the gap between the best and worst locations, coach partners to a standard customers can count on, and build the mechanisms that lift the whole network at once.

Our culture is hands-on, data-driven, and high-ownership. We obsess over the customer, thrive in ambiguity, dive deep into the details on the ground, and think big about how to scale what works — because the best decisions about in-store returns are made by people who've seen them happen firsthand.

We are looking for a highly driven, entrepreneurial, analytical and customer-obsessed individual join the Business Development team in Italy. You will join the team selling Amazon Shipping services and will be responsible for developing a strong pipeline of the largest companies in Italy, detect opportunities, negotiate with external companies and close sales, as well as collecting market segment and customer insights to improve the product and delight the Amazon customers.

You are the ideal candidate if:
• You are excited by contributing to launching and developing a new business
• You are passionate about collaborating with different teams: Marketing, Customer Programs, Operations, Legal, etc.
• You have a proven track record in sales, and executing to meet or exceed these goals
• You excel at establishing top level relationships with customers, and are able to assess their needs, and work to find the best solutions for them
• You are a self-starter and can juggle multiple priorities to make things happen in a fast-paced, dynamic, and highly ambiguous environment
• You have experience in developing trustful relationships with external and internal stakeholders, including key accounts and teams across Operations, Procurement, Finance, Legal
• You can easily shift between strategic thinking and rolling up your sleeves and executing, in order to deliver results

• Leadership: be part of the organization’s leadership team and help implementing the overall strategy and direction

• Cross-functional collaboration: work with operations, product, and tech leaders to manage the program and build a product that fits the needs of customers
• Dive deep: Measure performance, identify gaps and opportunities, and lead the team to address them
• Business development: Bring new customers to Amazon, develop the volume of shipping packages, ensure good convertion rate and do it with profitability in mind.

This role will be based in Milan

target_jobs.description:
Si invitano a candidarsi persone appartenenti alle Categorie Protette ai sensi della L.68/99

AWS Infrastructure Services gestisce la progettazione, la pianificazione, la consegna e il funzionamento di tutta l'infrastruttura globale AWS. In altre parole, siamo le persone che mantengono il cloud operativo. Supportiamo tutti i data center AWS e tutti i server, lo storage, le apparecchiature di rete, alimentazione e raffreddamento che garantiscono ai nostri clienti l'accesso continuo all'innovazione su cui fanno affidamento. Lavoriamo sui problemi più complessi, con migliaia di variabili che influenzano la supply chain — e stiamo cercando persone di talento che vogliono aiutarci.

I Logistics Secialist monitorano i livelli di inventario per garantire che vengano mantenuti livelli di stock adeguati a supportare le attività di costruzione e riparazione. Ricevono componenti, gestiscono l'inventario e distribuiscono componenti secondo necessità ai tecnici e agli ingegneri del Data Center. Sono responsabili del carico e scarico delle spedizioni e del trasporto di componenti tra diverse sedi.

Questa posizione comporta il sollevamento frequente di materiali e prodotti. I Logistics Secialist sono tenuti a mantenere registrazioni precise di tutte le merci in entrata e in uscita dall'azienda.

Cerchiamo candidati che possiedano una forte etica del lavoro, attenzione ai dettagli, capacità di rispettare le scadenze e un impegno verso la Sicurezza e l'Eccellenza Operativa.

Key job responsibilities
• Revisione dell'inventario del Data Center, delle spedizioni in entrata e della domanda continua per garantire che vengano mantenuti livelli di stock adeguati in tutte le sedi a supporto delle attività di costruzione e riparazione.
• Collaborazione con il Logistics Manager per creare piani per ottimizzare il flusso di componenti durante il loro ciclo di vita; tracciamento della posizione, movimento, età e rotazione dell'inventario.
• Stretta collaborazione con i tecnici e gli ingegneri del Data Center per fornire componenti rapidamente e con precisione.
• Collaborazione con Procurement e Hardware Engineering per acquistare nuovi componenti e interfacciarsi direttamente con i fornitori per elaborare RMA e ricevere sostituzioni.
• Mantenimento di dashboard metriche aggiornate e creazione di report per fornitori interni ed esterni e per il management secondo necessità.
• Assemblaggio, indirizzamento, preparazione e organizzazione della spedizione di merci e materiali.
• Assistenza nella programmazione giornaliera delle consegne e dei ritiri da e verso le varie località.
• Mantenimento di registrazioni precise di tutte le merci in entrata e in uscita dall'azienda.

SICUREZZA:
• I Logistics Secialist devono comprendere tutti gli aspetti della produzione, aderire a rigorosi standard di sicurezza, mantenere livelli molto elevati di qualità.

REQUISITI FISCI:
• Richiesta movimentazione manuale e sollevamento di attrezzature (limiti di peso in conformità con le normative)
• Gestione delle spedizioni in arrivo, disimballaggio di scatole e verifica del contenuto • Lavoro in aree rumorose con temperature più calde e più fredde rispetto alle condizioni ambientali standard degli uffici

SEDE DI LAVORO:
I nostri data center si trovano in aree remote fuori Milano, dove l'accesso tramite trasporto pubblico può essere limitato. Pertanto, è richiesta una patente di guida UE valida e un veicolo personale per questo ruolo.

A day in the life
Esperienze Diverse
AWS valorizza le esperienze diverse. Anche se non soddisfi tutte le qualifiche e competenze preferite elencate nella descrizione del lavoro, incoraggiamo i candidati a candidarsi. Se la tua carriera è appena iniziata, non ha seguito un percorso tradizionale o include esperienze alternative, non lasciare che questo ti impedisca di candidarti.

Perché AWS?
Amazon Web Services (AWS) è la piattaforma cloud più completa e ampiamente adottata al mondo. Abbiamo aperto la strada al cloud computing e non abbiamo mai smesso di innovare — ecco perché i clienti, dalle startup di maggior successo alle aziende Global 500, si affidano alla nostra robusta suite di prodotti e servizi per alimentare le loro attività.

Cultura di Team Inclusiva
Qui in AWS, è nella nostra natura imparare ed essere curiosi. I nostri gruppi di affinità guidati dai dipendenti promuovono una cultura di inclusione che ci consente di essere orgogliosi delle nostre differenze. Eventi continui ed esperienze di apprendimento, incluse le nostre conferenze Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) e AmazeCon (diversità di genere), ci ispirano a non smettere mai di abbracciare la nostra unicità.

Mentorship e Crescita Professionale
Stiamo continuamente alzando il nostro standard di performance mentre ci sforziamo di diventare il Miglior Datore di Lavoro. Ecco perché troverai infinite risorse di condivisione della conoscenza, mentorship e altre risorse per l'avanzamento di carriera qui per aiutarti a svilupparti in un professionista più completo.

Equilibrio Lavoro/Vita
Valorizziamo l'armonia tra lavoro e vita privata. Raggiungere il successo sul lavoro non dovrebbe mai avvenire a spese di sacrifici a casa, motivo per cui ci impegniamo per la flessibilità come parte della nostra cultura lavorativa. Quando ci sentiamo supportati sul posto di lavoro e a casa, non c'è nulla che non possiamo realizzare nel cloud.

Il team
Ti unirai a un team diversificato di ingegneri software, hardware e di rete, specialisti della supply chain, esperti di sicurezza, operations manager e altri ruoli vitali. Collaborerai con persone in tutta AWS per aiutarci a fornire i più alti standard di sicurezza e protezione fornendo al contempo una capacità apparentemente infinita al costo più basso possibile per i nostri clienti. E sperimenterai una cultura inclusiva che accoglie idee audaci e ti dà il potere di portarle a compimento.

Please note: This job is advertised for Luxembourg but can be located in any of our EU sites or offices.

We are seeking a Senior Analyst to own the analytical backbone across multiple high-impact domains within EU Inbound Supply Chain. This is not a single-metric reporting role you will design scalable data architectures, build production-grade analytics systems, and drive strategic decisions through data, working across both real-time streaming and batch processing to get the team the right data at the right time.

The ideal candidate pairs deep technical expertise in data engineering and analytics with the ability to influence cross-functional stakeholders and turn ambiguous business problems into measurable solutions. You're equally comfortable building scalable pipelines on AWS services over terabytes of data, architecting a real-time monitoring solution, presenting to senior leadership, or prototyping GenAI tools to scale analytical capacity.

What makes this role unique:
- Context-switching is the job - one week you're decomposing a delivery-accuracy variance across the EU network; the next you're building a real-time Inbound Management pipeline; the week after you're prototyping a GenAI tool that auto-generates root-cause narratives for business reviews.
- Federated stakeholder model - you'll work across Engineering, Science, Transportation, Planning, Finance, and Operations. Aligning on definitions and building shared analytical frameworks matters as much as writing the code.
- GenAI as a force multiplier - you won't just use AI tools, you'll build them: agentic deep-dives, automated narrative generation, and intelligent alerting that scale analysis across inbound speed, DEA, and transportation optimization.


Key job responsibilities
- Design and own end-to-end data architectures spanning real-time streaming (Kinesis, Flink) and batch processing (EMR, Redshift, Athena), selecting the right paradigm for the latency, volume, and criticality at hand.
- Build production-grade, scalable ETL/ELT pipelines processing multi-TB datasets daily across Redshift, Athena, S3, and DynamoDB with data-quality checks, monitoring, and alerting.
- Architect real-time analytics for operational monitoring: live visibility into inbound flows, delivery accuracy, dock congestion, and network disruptions.
- Own metric frameworks and reporting: design KPIs, build automated dashboards (QuickSight), support WBR/MBR narratives, and own the “why” through root-cause analysis when metrics move.
- Develop GenAI-driven tooling and agentic workflows that automate reporting narratives and root-cause analysis, reducing time-to-insight from days to minutes.
- Drive deep-dive investigations across complex, multi-source datasets tracing issues to specific products, warehouses, or routes, then quantifying network-wide impact with statistical methods.



A day in the life
You'll have exposure to the full data-product lifecycle — from defining metrics to designing architectures, building pipelines, and delivering insights to senior leadership. A typical week might include:
- Designing pipelines that unify real-time event streams (shipment scans, trailer movements, inventory updates) and batch sources (forecasts, historical performance) into a single analytical layer.
- Writing advanced SQL across multiple sources to investigate why delivery promises were missed from the customer order through placement, transportation, and fulfillment.
- Building Python-based automation for anomaly detection, statistical modeling, and reporting.
- Iterating on GenAI-powered tools and presenting data-driven recommendations, with clear quantification of customer and cost impact, to senior leadership.
- Triaging emerging operational issues from real-time dashboards and providing data-backed context.

About the team
The Global Operational Excellence (GOX) team drives operational improvements across Amazon’s EU fulfillment network and ROW. We work at the intersection of technology and operations to optimize how inventory is placed, moved, and delivered reducing costs while improving customer experience. Our team leverages large-scale data analysis, automation, and cross-functional collaboration to solve complex supply chain challenges across Inbound Speed, Delivery Estimate Accuracy (DEA), and network performance.

As an analyst in the Long Term Planning (LTP) - Middle Mile Analytics team, you will be responsible for creating robust and explainable plans which determine the future of Amazon’s outbound Middle Mile (MM) network in Europe. We use modeling and analysis to project MM flows and KPIs for a 1 to 3+ year time horizon, driving decisions on savings initiatives, network connectivity, productivity and Sort Center topology. We operate in a cross-functional environment, planning alongside other miles and interacting closely with partners across finance, SCOT, ATS and STEP network design teams.

This is a highly visible position that requires interacting with multiple business teams, collaborating with tech teams, and interaction with senior leaders. The day to day activities consist of approximately 30% stakeholder/project management and 70% analytical activities.

Key job responsibilities
* Collecting and auditing model inputs, working with external stakeholders to understand the reasons for changes
* Running and configuring analytical models to produce network plans
* Auditing model outputs to ensure quality and explainability of plans
* Solving new and ambiguous planning problems as they arise; sometimes under time pressure
* Contributing to the documentation and presentation of modeling results
* Contributing to the continuous improvement of planning models and processes, working with TPMs and BIEs

About the team
- Operations is at the heart of the Amazon customer experience. Each action we undertake is on behalf of our customers, as surpassing their expectations is our passion. We improve customer experience through continuously optimizing the complex movements of goods from vendors to customers throughout Europe.
- The Supply Chain, Transportation Planning & Operational Excellence (EU STEP) is a team responsible for the end-to-end flow of goods from our vendors and sellers to Amazon customers all over Europe, in order to ensure a speedy and reliable customer delivery in the cheapest way possible.

We work with operations teams, Retail and FBA, finance, tech teams to improve our ability to serve customers with faster speed and at lower cost.

target_jobs.description:
Are you passionate about safety and ready to drive meaningful change at a global scale? Join our team as a Workplace, Health, and Safety (WHS) Program Manager and play a pivotal role in protecting the people who power Amazon's worldwide operations.

In this role, you'll serve as a trusted safety partner to senior regional and regional leaders, ensuring world-class safety standards for Information Technology (IT) team members across Amazon's global network. Through regular site visits, you'll stay closely connected to the daily realities of our frontline technicians — translating those insights into impactful regional and global safety programs.

You will own and drive safety programs from inception through implementation, lead rigorous incident investigations to uncover root causes, and develop corrective actions that prevent recurrence. You'll also design and execute safety campaigns that embed a culture of ownership and accountability across the business.

Collaborating cross-functionally with Operations, Engineering, HR, and beyond, you'll scale successful safety initiatives and help cement Amazon's reputation as an industry safety leader.

Key job responsibilities
- Own and drive safety programs from inception through global implementation, delivering measurable risk reduction outcomes across Amazon's worldwide network
- Lead and manage safety-related projects end-to-end, defining clear actions, owners, and timelines to ensure successful delivery
- Author narrative papers and business reviews for senior leadership audiences, clearly communicating safety priorities, program performance, and investment recommendations
- Solve complex safety challenges faced by IT employees, including work at heights, hazardous energy, and battery safety, developing scalable solutions that reduce risk across the organization
- Serve as a trusted safety partner to regional leaders, aligning on strategic priorities and tracking progress against goals
- Conduct regular site visits to distribution centers, sortation facilities, and delivery stations to personally observe safety practices, gather frontline feedback, and identify opportunities for improvement
- Develop and update regional and global safety standards, protocols, and training materials informed by site visit insights, driving consistent, best-in-class safety performance
- Lead comprehensive incident investigations, rapidly identifying root causes and implementing corrective actions to prevent recurrence and share learnings globally
- Collaborate cross-functionally with teams in Operations, Engineering, HR, and beyond to scale successful safety initiatives and embed sustainable improvements
- Monitor safety metrics, analyze trends, and present data-driven recommendations to senior leadership on priorities and investment areas


A day in the life
Your day might begin with check-in calls with regional leaders across Europe to discuss emerging issues and align on priorities. You'll then join a global project call to review a battery end-of-life management narrative with teammates worldwide. In the afternoon, you lead an incident investigation — reviewing footage, interviewing witnesses, and mapping root causes. You may also partner with field leaders on action plans, design safety features for new equipment, or close the day analyzing a global safety dashboard to prepare data-driven recommendations for senior leadership.

About the team
The global WHS OpsTech Solutions team partners closely with Amazon's IT function, working to identify safety improvement opportunities by staying closely connected to the daily realities of our frontline technicians and end users. We collaborate cross-functionally to create policies, drive standardization, and enhance hardware — all with the goal of continuously improving procedural safety across the organization. By remaining grounded in the experiences of our workforce, we develop targeted solutions that protect our people and empower them to work safely. It's a dynamic, solutions-oriented group where we leverage our technical expertise and business acumen to make a real impact.

target_jobs.description:
Amazon's Fleet Procurement and Capacity Planning (FPAC) team manages a large-scale international commercial vehicle fleet across 10 European markets. This fleet depends on accurate, timely data flowing between two Fleet Management Companies (FMCs), Amazon's internal planning systems, and multiple cross-functional stakeholders.

This role owns the operational delivery and quality of all fleet data provided by FMCs (Ayvens and Arval) to Amazon. You will be the single-threaded owner ensuring that vehicle lifecycle data (from order placement through deployment, maintenance, defleeting, and remarketing) is delivered per contractual SLAs, meets validation standards, and flows reliably into the planning tools and reporting mechanisms that drive fleet capacity decisions.

This is a hands-on data operations and vendor management role. You will spend the majority of your time ensuring data reliability, resolving reporting failures with FMC technical contacts, and supporting the internal teams who depend on this data to make procurement and capacity decisions worth hundreds of millions in OPEX annually.

Please note that this is a 12 months fixed-term contract.

Key job responsibilities
1- Maintain Fleet Data Reliability
- Own the end-to-end data delivery relationship with Ayvens and Arval technical points of contact, ensuring reporting against established SLAs and contractual obligations
- Monitor, triage, and resolve data quality issues across SDR (Supply Delivery Reporting) and SRR (Supply Return Reporting) pipelines, including idle stock positions at VIN level
- Support Weekly Business Reviews and Variable Last Mile Rentals reporting cadences by ensuring upstream data is accurate and delivered on time
- Escalate systemic data failures through the appropriate FMC governance channels (Monthly Business Reviews, performance reviews).
2- Enable Planning Tools and Downstream Consumers
- Ensure data feeds into FORCE (Fleet Optimization, Requirement and Control Engine) and FAB (Fleet Allocation and Balancing) meet signal integration requirements
- Partner with the MAPS team (Mid-Term Planning) and Fleet Planning to resolve data gaps that block planning accuracy and automation
- Triage new data requests from internal stakeholders against existing data specifications; eliminate redundancy before placing additional requirements on FMCs
3- Drive Continuous Improvement

- Identify and implement process improvements to reduce manual data reconciliation effort
- Develop monitoring mechanisms to proactively flag reporting inaccuracies before they propagate into planning decisions
- Document and maintain the fleet data catalogue, including ownership, refresh cadences, quality thresholds, and known limitations
- Ensure any new fleet programs (LMR expansion, new country launches, Middle Mile integration) include data requirements in vendor agreements from the outset
4- Cross-Functional Coordination

- Align with Fleet Partnerships (FMC contractual owners), Fleet Deployment & Redeployment, Planning, and GFPA (Global Fleet Planning Analytics) on data priorities and dependencies
- Influence FMC behavior through performance metrics and contractual accountability rather than direct authority
- Represent data requirements in FMC governance forums (MBR/QBR)

Leaders are owners. They think long term for our customers and don’t sacrifice long-term value for short-term results. Amazon Freight Europe is looking for just such an owner to lead the strategy for our externalized freight business to design and deliver a world class freight experience for our business customers.

ABOUT THIS ROLE
The Head of Strategy will report directly into the leader of the Amazon Freight Europe business to lead and build out the newly created Strategy team across Europe (including UK). They will be based in Luxembourg, London or Munich to tackle the most hotly debated topics within our startup organization. They will partner closely with Product, Program, Operations and Commercial leaders to identify the challenges and opportunities in our organization, and come up with creative, customer-driven solutions to solve them. The Head of Strategy will work across both the European business and worldwide tech domains to shape our long-term business plan, diving deep with leaders across multiple areas to define customer problems and deliver the solutions.

ABOUT YOU
You’re a self-described ‘builder’ and ‘fixer’ with a passion for figuring out what the future looks like. You have a relentless focus on creating and improving customer value. You’re a hands-on multitasker who can quickly change focus and balance the needs of the moment with longer-term goals. You have a high tolerance for ambiguity and complexity. You have resilience and a positive, solutions-oriented attitude – even the toughest challenges are possible with the right amount of creativity, good judgment and hard work. You have strong problem solving, communication and organizational skills and the ability to influence stakeholders without direct authority, along with a good understanding of product development/management and digital media.

You’re a leader with a blend of strategy, product management and/or operations experience and have the business acumen to understand and shape Amazon Freight’s business-wide roadmap. You achieve your results through other people, often without authority, making complex decisions simple through data and inspire people at all levels in the organization. You proactively identify gaps and risks, and partner with senior leaders in and out of the organization to define creative solutions to solve them. You embody the rare combination of thinker and doer.

YOU WILL.
-Partner with Product, Program, Operations and Commercial teams to oversee strategic business initiatives from development through to successful execution, ensuring that individual function targets are in harmony and resolving those that aren’t.
Support colleagues in their decision-making, program management, and initiative implementation, calling out opportunities to double-down and the unseen risks.
-Review, design, and execute improvements to organizational structure; find knowledge and skills gaps and help address them.
-Improve current processes and review organization-wide procedures for efficiency and productivity.
-Control the output of shared-services functions to ensure that outsourced tasks deliver to the high expectations of our Amazon Freight customers.

Key job responsibilities
•Ensure department goals are well integrated with each other and control organization-wide success, identifying areas to invest, double down or repair.
•Influence wider Amazon teams to secure collaborative, efficient solutions for our customers, re-using existing capabilities wherever possible.
•Build long term strategic plans, working alongside our product team, who specifies new products and features, our tech team that builds them, our operations that deliver them, our commercial team that sells them as well as the Amazon Freight teams outside EU.
•Stay close to the operational realities of our business, recognizing that what we will build has its foundation in the work of our Associates and partners on sites and in vehicles.
•This includes organizational design to help build our future team structures whilst securing support to our team for new hires, including documentation, onboarding, and learning and development team.

We apply the same customer obsession that we are known for in the consumer business to the Business to Business segment, aiming to partner with our customers to meet the demands of today while helping to navigate the road ahead. The team is diverse and intercultural with passionate members with a team-focused attitude. Across Amazon, we have committed to reach net-zero carbon by 2040, ten years ahead of the Paris Agreement and we take this commitment seriously in Amazon Freight too. We’re not there yet but if this sounds interesting, maybe you can help us get there.

target_jobs.description:
Amazon’s European Transportation Network Design team is responsible for getting Amazon packages to customers more reliably, faster, cheaper, and with a lower carbon intensity, while managing to grow the shipped volume by double digits every year.

We are looking for Program Manager for Network Design, you'll lead programs driving strategic initiatives and solving recurring problems around delivery quality, speed, cost and carbon intensity of the Amazon Transportation network in EU . Your goal is not just to solve problems once, but also to build new tools and improve processes to make sure the problems stay solved. This is essential to the scalability of the Amazon Transportation Network.

Do you recognize yourself in this?
• You are data-driven and enjoy analyzing large quantities of data and turning them into crisp insights
• You are an excellent problem solver, with a demonstrated ability to bring structure to complex projects and break them down into smaller pieces
• You are able to deliver projects against tight deadlines and are comfortable with competing priorities.
• You get energy from finding root causes for recurring problems and inventing new tools and processes to avoid them.
• You are eager to learn about the complexities of Amazon's transportation network and the systems that support it. At the same time, you have the communication skills to explain this to someone without subject matter expertise.
• You are able to coordinate multiple cross-functional projects in parallel across Tech, Operations, Supply Chain and Finance.
• You have a drive to constantly learn and improve yourself
• You can translate strategic directions into a project roadmap and build the resourcing plan to deliver on this roadmap

Then this is a role for you! We're looking forward to your application.

The position is based in Amazon’s European headquarters in Luxembourg, a city widely known for its beautiful setting, livability, and highly international population with foreign nationals making up over half of the population.


Key job responsibilities
Define the frameworks to make trade-offs between quality, speed, cost and carbon intensity
Find situations in the network where these tradeoffs are not applied correctly, leading to an inefficient network
Build a proof of concept to solve the problem initially
Work with Business Intelligence / Software Development to automate the methodology
Set up the mechanism to regularly review the gaps in optimality and suggest network changes to make sure the problem stays fixed


About the team
Our team changes the way Amazon packages get from our warehouses to our customers to improve quality, speed, cost and carbon efficiency, all at the same time, while managing double-digit yearly volume growth.

We launch new buildings, help Amazon get ready for the Christmas period and tackle big recurring problems, all to remove waste from the network.

This role tagged as one of Amazon’s Supply Chain Managers play a central role in our global business. They keep our complex, international supply chains working seamlessly and efficiently. As a Supply Chain Manager (SCM), you will work closely with multiple stakeholders across Amazon, from Operational teams who are fulfilling customer orders to Retail teams and everything in between. You’ll help us optimise our supply chains to make our customer experience even better and our business more energy and cost efficient.


Key job responsibilities
Define the Amazon outbound network planning (Legs, Sorts, CPT) for one of the UK sub-regions covered by 3-5 Sort Centers.
Analyse the best design based on forecast, and historical flows to improve cost, speed and DEA across E2E network.
Partner with teams to align on network changes to solve operational challenges.
Support the planning and organization of complex projects including Peak network transformations

A day in the life
Being a Network Manager for Amazon involves lots of problem solving. You’ll work with a number of teams to navigate challenges as and when situations impact our network. You’ll spend time resolving temporary issues and looking at the bigger picture to drive Amazon towards achieving new objectives. This role is both proactive and reactive, and you’ll have the opportunity to help forecast and plan for new projects.

As a Supply Chain Manager, you’ll need to help with both on-the-ground tasks and more tactical work. No two days will be the same. You could spend one day helping to define our supply chain and operating models and the next assisting with a site’s resource plan for a busy period. Having so much variety in your role means you’ll be able to learn something new every day.

This role is based in Luxembourg headquarters.

About the team
Amazon couldn’t deliver at pace without the STEP TNO team. As part of STEP TNO MMNC, you’ll be welcomed into a diverse team that plays a central role in our success. Using air, sea and road transport, as well as sortation centres equipped with the latest technology, you’ll help Amazon’s transport run at maximum efficiency. Our team captures data and uses it to drive decisions. They are key to making Amazon more innovative and efficient.
We put safety first as our people are our priority. And we use the expertise of our people to get packages to their destination – quickly, conveniently and sustainably.

target_jobs.description:
Are you inspired by invention? Is problem solving through teamwork in your DNA? Do you like the idea of seeing how your work impacts the bigger picture? Answer yes to any of these and you’ll fit right in here at Amazon Robotics. We are a smart team of doers that work passionately to apply the latest advances in robotics and software to solve real-world challenges that will transform our customers’ experiences in ways we can’t even imagine yet. We invent new improvements every day. We are Amazon Robotics and we will give you the tools and guidance you need to invent with us in ways that are rewarding, fulfilling and fun.

Our diverse teams come from all over the world to design, test and build our dynamic fleet of robots, mechatronic systems and pack automation solutions. Having our offices, labs, test floors and factories all co-located means that we can design the hardware, write the code, test, build and watch it all come to life. This allows us to innovate quickly and on limitless ideas. Current advancements are underway in autonomous movement and mobility, artificial intelligence and machine learning, manipulation, simulation, robotic management software, predictive analytics, and much more.

We are seeking Robotics Supply Chain New Product Lead - Tech tackle to most critical, technologically advanced products at Amazon. The Lead will be responsible for a small portfolio of robotic products and accountable for supplier and supply chain strategies, product cost roadmaps, enabling rapid NPI builds, and ensuring a successful ramp to mass production. They manage their products from concept, through development, to scaled deployment. They work with senior product and engineering leaders to drive appropriate trade-offs between commercial vs. technical constraints, risks and goals. Within the robotic product they lead, they must be able to drive the multiple advanced technologies and commodities, driving a clear path to production.

Essential to the role is a level of technical subject matter expertise to work effectively with the technical teams developing these robotic products. While it varies by group, this expertise includes an understanding of the technologies and architectures of the robotic products and key commodities that make up the robotic products, including the technology’s development and integration strategy and trajectory, both within Amazon and its wider position in the business and industry. This role will contribute to technical strategies and decisions, with contributions that balance technical and business requirements, to help drive engineering teams toward scalable products that achieve Amazon’s cost targets.

Alternate Job location - ANR10 (Hamme) can be considered for this role


Key job responsibilities
The RSC New Product Lead - Tech is a trusted subject matter expert, consulted by teams above and below. They clearly communicate with direct and indirect stakeholders, advocating for commercial opportunities at the Director level and above. They contribute to strategic documents for aligning goals with cross-functional teams, own reporting on forecasting and planning the business impact of each opportunity, and regularly report on the status and impact of their contributions. Their impact is measurable via quantifiable metrics, and they have the ability to deeply influence measurable business outcomes.


- Lead Product Development Process working cross-functional supply chain team dedicated to the supplier, supply chain design, sourcing, logistics decisions, and supply chain execution for robotics products from concept, through development, to scaled deployment.
- Act as single point of contact for program resources (leadership and working teams) to communicate Supply Chain decisions and progress, provide feedback on supply chain implications of program decisions and changes, and support financial planning and capital approvals for the program.
- Work with Robotics leadership to ensure partnership between Robotics Supply Chain, hardware engineering, operations and program teams on commodity and supplier selection, cost performance tradeoff analysis, cost road map development and execution, and enabling rapid product development stages, and delivering an effective path to scaled deployment.
- Responsible for definition and approval of the Product level Supply Chain Strategy documents, including identification of critical components and suppliers, product cost roadmap to meet payback targets, definition of capacity plan and associated sourcing and tooling requirements, supply chain risk assessment & mitigation plans.
- Work with sourcing in developing negotiation strategies for categories which impacts the product to deliver against business objectives and achieve sustainable relationships with strategic suppliers pertaining to Amazon Robotics products supporting the priority programs as driven by the Operating Plan (OP)
- Work with GCMs on managing overall supplier relationships including supplier performance, capability development, capacity planning, contracting, risk mitigation, and cost and quality improvements.
- Develop roadmap to achieving total cost targets (TCO), including make vs. buy analysis and value engineering opportunities
- Ensure non-cost goals (Sustainability, Supplier Development, Cost Savings) are met and supported by the product specific supply chain strategy.
- Travel internationally across Europe for around 20-25% of the time.

A day in the life
The NPI STL orchestrates new product introduction across Amazon Robotics' supply chain.
A typical day involves leading PDP gate reviews, aligning DfX requirements with engineering teams, and driving supply chain readiness for hardware programs. Internal stakeholders include mechanical/electrical engineers, sourcing managers, manufacturing partners, and program managers. Customers are the robotics product lines launching new systems. The role solves problems at the intersection of design and supply — ensuring parts are sourceable, manufacturable, and available on time. Expect cross-functional stand-ups, supplier escalations, regionalization strategy sessions, and risk reviews tracking critical path components to production milestones.

About the team
The Amazon Robotics Supply Chain team provides strategic sourcing for a portfolio of robotic technologies and is responsible for delivering new products by enabling the right suppliers and technologies, and getting the right materials at the right cost to the right place at the right time to support our network of global fulfillment and transportation solutions. It is a fast-paced operation that works cross-functionally with teams across Amazon and is driven by data and metrics.

The NPI Supply Chain Product Management team develops supply chain strategies for new Fulfillment Tech and Robotics products from concept to general availability. As the central integration point between technical, commercial, and operational teams, we drive PDP adherence and comprehensive supplier readiness oversight. Our vision establishes scalable, cost-effective solutions leveraging AI-driven insights to exceed performance targets. Our mission encompasses end-to-end strategy development through data-driven decisions, comprehensive make-vs-buy frameworks, regional manufacturing strategies, and cross-functional integration with partner ops teams. We maintain accountability for product cost targets, supplier readiness metrics, and program milestones while optimizing total landed cost and operational efficiency across FTR's portfolio.

target_jobs.description:
Would you like to build technology products that help shape Amazon’s transition toward a more circular economy? Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) regulations are rapidly changing how producers and retailers manage products and packaging after sale, including recycling obligations, fees, reporting, seller compliance, and reverse logistics. Amazon is building the technology and operating mechanisms required to manage these obligations at global scale while creating the foundation for broader circularity services.

As a Principal Product Manager – Technical, you will define and lead the product strategy for some of Amazon’s most complex sustainability and regulatory challenges. You will work across engineering, science, compliance, finance, operations, and sustainability teams to automate global EPR programs, improve product and packaging data, enable compliant selling partners, and develop scalable capabilities for recycling, recovery, and circularity.

This role requires a product leader who can operate in significant ambiguity, translate evolving regulatory and business requirements into durable technical solutions, and influence across a broad set of senior stakeholders. You will help determine where Amazon should build common global platforms versus localized solutions, establish mechanisms that improve accuracy and reduce manual effort, and shape new services that can support both compliance and circular-economy objectives.

This is a high-visibility opportunity to build at the intersection of technology, regulation, sustainability, and Amazon-scale commerce, with the ability to influence how Amazon manages producer responsibility today and how it develops broader circularity capabilities for the future.

Key job responsibilities
-Define and deliver AI-enabled products that scale global EPR compliance, including monitoring emerging regulations and policy changes, translating requirements into product and control strategies, and enabling rapid expansion across new geographies and regulatory use cases.
-Improve the Selling Partner compliance experience by building products that make requirements easier to understand and act on, reduce the effort and cost required to achieve compliance, and enable sellers to continue offering products across Amazon stores.
Own the multi-year product strategy and roadmap for EPR and circular economy, leading 3-Year Vision, annual operating planning, and quarterly prioritization while aligning investments across business, technology, compliance, sustainability, and operations teams.
-Drive automation and simplification across Amazon’s EPR operating model, replacing manual processes with scalable technology, improving data and classification accuracy, and strengthening controls across reporting, fees, registrations, and compliance monitoring.
-Develop new circular-economy capabilities and services across recycling, recovery, reverse logistics, and producer accountability, identifying opportunities where Amazon can meet regulatory requirements while improving customer and Selling Partner experiences.
-Influence and align senior cross-functional leaders across engineering, science, finance, legal, public policy, operations, and sustainability to resolve ambiguous problems, make investment tradeoffs, and deliver durable global solutions.

In this role, you will own the end-to-end planning and execution for the Same Day network across Micro Fulfillment Centers (MFCs). You will dive deep into data to identify opportunities, solve complex supply chain problems, and drive improvements that directly impact delivery speed and customer satisfaction.

This is a role that blends short-term operational execution with long-term strategic planning. You will work with incomplete data, make high-judgment decisions, and collaborate across multiple teams to shape the future of Same Day delivery in Europe.

Key job responsibilities

5- Drive strategic projects that improve cost efficiency, delivery speed, and network scalability
6- Partner cross-functionally with Delivery Stations, Fulfillment Centers, Speed, and Finance teams to align on network plans and drive operational excellence.
7- Communicate insights and recommendations to senior leadership, influencing long-term network strategy


About the team
Customer Fulfilment, or CF, is where it all started for Amazon. CF has scaled up from a humble team of booksellers to a sophisticated global team which handles more than 1.5 million orders every day. The team is the foundation of our business and its efforts have helped us diversify across new regions and services. With the help of emerging technology, we’re always looking for ways to offer a bigger, better product range – delivered quickly and affordably.

The CF team are the first people in the chain that helps customers get products at the speed we’re known for. We’re based in Fulfilment Centres, which are at the heart of Amazon’s fast-paced Operations network. Our centres are sometimes referred to as the ‘First Mile’ because it’s where most Amazon packages start their journey. We help to manage dynamic inventory and facilitate speedy deliveries round the clock.

Our candidate should be passionate about using data to solve big, complex, and ambiguous problems across end-to-end network design - spanning Inbound, Sortable, Non-Sort, Middle Mile, and Last Mile segments.
The ideal candidate should be eager to continuously learn and improve their skills, with a keen eye for the details that make all the difference. You will partner with network planning teams to drive financial governance, support multi-billion euro CapEx planning, and shape the topology decisions that define how we serve customers faster.
Do you want to contribute to shaping the future of logistics and the new standard of shopping? If so, come and join the Network Planning Finance team.

Key job responsibilities
- Independently identifies and drives cost-out opportunities across multiple network segments (Inbound, Sortable, Non-Sort, Middle Mile, Last Mile) by connecting operational performance metrics to financial outcomes, defining the analytical framework where one may not exist

- Navigates complex, ambiguous CapEx and network cost structures with limited or incomplete data, exercising senior judgement to size opportunities, quantify trade-offs, and recommend action to leadership with confidence

- Leads root cause analysis on systemic issues spanning multiple sites or topology decisions, uncovering underlying drivers and designing scalable measurement frameworks that raise the bar on network efficiency

- Serves as a trusted strategic partner to senior Network Planning leaders, proactively influencing decisions on investment, capacity placement, and network cost strategy rather than responding to requests

- Owns the end-to-end relationship with data source providers and technology teams, driving automation roadmaps, defining data quality standards, and ensuring decision-grade data is available at pace to support network design cycles

- Identifies and champions process improvements across the wider finance organization, codifying best practices, raising the analytical standard for peers and junior analysts

A day in the life
You will be at the heart of how Amazon's logistics network evolves. On any given day, you might be building the financial business case for a new site launch, modelling what happens to cost and service when a topology change is proposed, or presenting capacity investment trade-offs to Senior Leadership.
You will partner closely with Network Planning, Operations, and Technology teams to translate complex planning decisions into clear financial recommendations. One morning you could be quantifying the cost impact of adding a new node to the network; by the afternoon, you may be automating a reporting pipeline using AI tools to free up time for deeper analysis.
No two days look the same, but the thread that ties them together is this: you will use data, judgement, and financial rigor to help the business make better, faster decisions about where to invest, what to build, and how to design the network of the future.

About the team
As part of the End-to-end Network Design Finance team, you will join a team that is passionate about numbers, data, and how to use them to generate insights and improve our business. We support and influence the organization by providing a holistic and financial perspective, we are the trusted business advisors. We collaborate with our partners to ensure leaders have the most up to date and reliable information, and work with them to make sure we are making the best possible decisions.

target_jobs.description:
Amazon is looking for a Senior Product Manager to own the EU Digital Product Passport (DPP) product end-to-end. The DPP is a foundational regulatory obligation under the EU Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation (ESPR) — and a significant strategic opportunity for Amazon. As product owner, you will define the vision and roadmap and translate a fast-moving regulatory landscape into concrete product requirements.
This is a builder role for someone who thrives in ambiguity. The problem space is not fully defined: regulations are still being finalized, harmonised technical standards are emerging, and Amazon’s approach must be invented from first principles. You will set the goals, make the one-way and two-way door calls, and drive clarity across teams that have competing priorities. You will hold an honest tension between what the regulation requires and what creates durable value for customers and the business.
Success looks like: a defensible product strategy grounded in the regulation; a data pipeline and attribute framework that scale across product categories; on-time delivery of mandatory obligations; and DPP data positioned as a reusable asset that unlocks value across Amazon beyond pure compliance.

Key job responsibilities
* Own the DPP product vision, strategy, and roadmap.
* Translate regulation into product requirements.
* Shape the DPP data pipeline alongside engineering.
* Manage stakeholders and communicate with precision.
* Own DPP metrics and reporting.
* Extend DPP value beyond compliance.
* Operate AI-first. Encode product judgment, tenets, and trade-off frameworks into durable, machine-readable artifacts, and use AI to compress research, synthesis, and drafting cycles — owning the outcome and applying judgment to what ships.

About the team
The EU Digital Product Passport team sits within Amazon RISC International and owns Amazon’s response to one of the most consequential product-compliance shifts in the EU. A Digital Product Passport is a structured, verifiable record of a product’s attributes — origin, composition, sustainability, and circularity data — accessible via a data carrier such as a QR code. Under ESPR and its delegated acts, DPPs become mandatory on a rolling schedule by product category, starting with batteries and extending to textiles, toys, and beyond.
Beyond the regulatory mandate, the team is charting how DPP data can become a strategic asset across Amazon — for example, powering Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) eco-modulation, enriching the catalog, and serving as a single source of truth that auto-populates downstream compliance requirements. The person in this role helps define that ambition and turn it into a shippable roadmap.

We are seeking a Senior Analyst to own the analytical backbone across multiple high-impact domains within EU Inbound Supply Chain. This is not a single-metric reporting role you will design scalable data architectures, build production-grade analytics systems, and drive strategic decisions through data, working across both real-time streaming and batch processing to get the team the right data at the right time.

The ideal candidate pairs deep technical expertise in data engineering and analytics with the ability to influence cross-functional stakeholders and turn ambiguous business problems into measurable solutions. You're equally comfortable building scalable pipelines on AWS services over terabytes of data, architecting a real-time monitoring solution, presenting to senior leadership, or prototyping GenAI tools to scale analytical capacity.

What makes this role unique:
- Context-switching is the job - one week you're decomposing a delivery-accuracy variance across the EU network; the next you're building a real-time Inbound Management pipeline; the week after you're prototyping a GenAI tool that auto-generates root-cause narratives for business reviews.
- Federated stakeholder model - you'll work across Engineering, Science, Transportation, Planning, Finance, and Operations. Aligning on definitions and building shared analytical frameworks matters as much as writing the code.
- GenAI as a force multiplier - you won't just use AI tools, you'll build them: agentic deep-dives, automated narrative generation, and intelligent alerting that scale analysis across inbound speed, DEA, and transportation optimization.


Key job responsibilities
- Design and own end-to-end data architectures spanning real-time streaming (Kinesis, Flink) and batch processing (EMR, Redshift, Athena), selecting the right paradigm for the latency, volume, and criticality at hand.
- Build production-grade, scalable ETL/ELT pipelines processing multi-TB datasets daily across Redshift, Athena, S3, and DynamoDB with data-quality checks, monitoring, and alerting.
- Architect real-time analytics for operational monitoring: live visibility into inbound flows, delivery accuracy, dock congestion, and network disruptions.
- Own metric frameworks and reporting: design KPIs, build automated dashboards (QuickSight), support WBR/MBR narratives, and own the “why” through root-cause analysis when metrics move.
- Develop GenAI-driven tooling and agentic workflows that automate reporting narratives and root-cause analysis, reducing time-to-insight from days to minutes.
- Drive deep-dive investigations across complex, multi-source datasets tracing issues to specific products, warehouses, or routes, then quantifying network-wide impact with statistical methods.



A day in the life
You'll have exposure to the full data-product lifecycle — from defining metrics to designing architectures, building pipelines, and delivering insights to senior leadership. A typical week might include:
- Designing pipelines that unify real-time event streams (shipment scans, trailer movements, inventory updates) and batch sources (forecasts, historical performance) into a single analytical layer.
- Writing advanced SQL across multiple sources to investigate why delivery promises were missed from the customer order through placement, transportation, and fulfillment.
- Building Python-based automation for anomaly detection, statistical modeling, and reporting.
- Iterating on GenAI-powered tools and presenting data-driven recommendations, with clear quantification of customer and cost impact, to senior leadership.
- Triaging emerging operational issues from real-time dashboards and providing data-backed context.

About the team
The Global Operational Excellence (GOX) team drives operational improvements across Amazon’s EU fulfillment network and ROW. We work at the intersection of technology and operations to optimize how inventory is placed, moved, and delivered reducing costs while improving customer experience. Our team leverages large-scale data analysis, automation, and cross-functional collaboration to solve complex supply chain challenges across Inbound Speed, Delivery Estimate Accuracy (DEA), and network performance.

Amazon's Inbound Long Term Planning team owns the topology framework that decides what the EU inbound network looks like in 2–3 years: which node types we build, where we place them, how they interact, and what inventory configuration they unlock. This role owns a critical slice of that framework — taking speed ambitions and placement targets and working backwards into the physical network design across 1DCs, RDCs, and IXDs that makes them achievable. It's the kind of problem where getting the answer right saves hundreds of millions of dollars; getting it wrong means we either over-invest or structurally cap our speed ceiling for years.

You'll work at the intersection of network topology, inventory science, and capital allocation — partnering deeply with Finance, IIPO, AIM, and business teams to determine the optimal long-term node configuration that delivers placement targets per outbound node type and selection cohort. This is a single-threaded role with high ambiguity and regular exposure to senior leadership across SCOT, Operations, and Finance.

Key job responsibilities
Key Job Responsibilities

- Own the long-term inbound topology framework — determine the optimal combination of node types, locations, and capacities that achieves placement targets at minimum total cost.

- Define network configuration per selection cohort — decide velocity demarcations between node types, regional zoning, and upstream storage share. Know when the model breaks and why.
- Build the multi-year inbound build plan — sequence node launches, size them against volume trajectories, and own the placement and inventory commitments that justify the investment.
- Resolve structural trade-offs that don't have clean owners. Frame options, quantify impact, and drive decisions when priorities across teams or geographies conflict.
- Align senior leadership to a single answer. Write the strategy documents that SCOT, Finance, IIPO, and Operations commit to. When priorities diverge, you reconcile.

Amazon Workplace Health & Safety (WHS) mission is to provide tools, resources, and environments that support safe, efficient, and healthy behaviors and encourage employees to proactively manage their health and wellbeing. To support this focus area, Amazon is seeking a leader to serve as our Program Manager for Worldwide WHS to build programs that create a safe workplace and build a world-class safety culture. In this role, you will dive deep into operations processes; identify risks through data and first-hand experience; build programs and improve processes to eliminate risks; and influence operations to sustain a culture of safety. This role will focus on leading large, strategic projects within Amazon Business Units (BU) and across different geographies – the role will also look for ways to replicate these BU-specific solutions to other BU, and find commonalities to support scale and speed.
The Sr. Program manager role will challenge you to push boundaries and lead transformative innovation while having the autonomy to make rapid data-driven decisions and invent on behalf of Operators (leaders) and Associates. In this role, you will work cross-functionally with members from various teams, including Operations; Amazon Fulfillment Technologies (AFT); Amazon Robotics (AR); Inbound Supply Chain; Launch; Sales & Operations Planning (S&OP); Capacity Planning; Finance and others to deploy solutions at scale.

This position requires travel up to approximately 25% when needed (and with appropriate health and safety conditions).



Key job responsibilities
The ideal candidate:
- Owns and drives safety programs from inception through global implementation, delivering measurable injury and risk reduction outcomes across Amazon's worldwide network.
- Leads and manages safety-related projects end-to-end, defining clear actions, owners, and timelines to ensure successful delivery.
- Authors narrative papers and business reviews for senior leadership audiences, clearly communicating safety priorities, program performance, and investment recommendations
- Serves as a trusted safety partner to regional leaders, aligning on strategic priorities and tracking progress against goals
- Conducts regular site visits to fulfillment centers, sortation facilities, and delivery stations to personally observe safety practices, gather front-line feedback, and identify opportunities for improvement
- Leads comprehensive incident investigations, rapidly identifying root causes and implementing corrective actions to prevent recurrence and share learnings globally
- Collaborates cross-functionally with teams in Operations, Engineering, HR, and beyond to scale successful safety initiatives and embed sustainable improvements
- Monitors safety metrics, analyze trends, and present data-driven recommendations to senior leadership on priorities and investment areas


A day in the life
As a Program Manager on the WHS Central Programs Team (CPT), your day centers on project management best practices applied to safety. Expect to spend your time reviewing safety data, running working sessions to unblock in-flight projects, and walking through operational processes to ground your decisions in field truth. You will drive projects that move from idea to validated, network-wide deployment, by working closely with BU stakeholders across the globe.

About the team
The WHS Central Programs Team (CPT) delivers projects that directly impact associate safety. target_jobs.description:
Reinvent how the world's largest robotics network gets deployed.
Amazon is seeking a Senior Manager for our Robotics Delivery, Packaging & Innovation to define and lead the Design for Deployment (DfD) technical deep-dive, and associated implementation strategy, across our global robotics fulfillment network. This is a founding, build-it-from-scratch role: you will define what "deployable" means for every robotics technology Amazon ships, and your decisions will shape how thousands of implementations happen across six continents.

Amazon's culture encourages an entrepreneurial approach and expects engineers and managers alike to take a high level of ownership in solving complex problems in a fast-paced environment.

The role could be based in Vercelli or alternatively in London or Luxembourg with ~60% travel across Europe and internationally for design reviews and field validation activities.

Key job responsibilities
This is a hands-on, boots-on-the-ground technical role. In the role you will:

- Serve as the organization's DfD technical authority, overview engineering drawings, mechatronic designs, and controls architectures, to embed quantified deployment requirements into engineering design, providing a single consolidated deployment voice and force multiplying deployment teams across multiple technology programs.
- Drive technically complex DfD programs: determining feasibility of infrastructure builds at scale, identifying when deployment issues stem from technical design decisions, and driving engineering to design to a defined deployment bar (mechanical, electrical, controls, layout, system integration and mechatronic domains).
- Advise VPs and the broader Robotics leadership on strategy, governance mechanisms and trade-offs, drive clarity where the problem itself may be undefined, optimize cross-organizational structures that enable teams to deliver independently.
- Coach deployment teams to engage in engineering design reviews, design decisions, and feed field learnings back to product teams systematically. You'll mentor deployment engineers and TiPMs, sharing DfD best practices and technical deep-dive methods and helping managers guide career growth.
- Define and own the end-to-end DfD strategy across all technology programs, ensuring every program has a quantified deployment bar (installation duration, workforce management, safety risk, cost per unit install).
- Force multiply deployment teams by creating, optimizing, and driving adoption of DfD mechanisms that enable teams to operate independently and at scale.
- Decompose complex deployment design problems into straightforward infrastructure solutions; define DfD Core Tenets and quantified requirements that engineering designs to across all solutions.
- Establish and evangelize the principle that deployment data is influence currency: creating systems and expectations for teams to document and quantify deployment pain caused by design decisions, replacing anecdotal feedback with systematic, data-driven design influence.
- Remediate critical and/or endemic deployment design problems; make trade-offs between business opportunity, resources, and sustainability with a long-term perspective.
- Identify endemic deployment problems, such as recurring modularity constraints, cable management challenges, or commissioning inefficiencies, diagnosing them and drive engineering to eliminate them at the source rather than compensating in the field.
- Drive measurable DfD outcomes and metrics, such as reduction in deployment duration, cost per unit, first-time installation success rate.

A day in the life
As a Sr. Manager, you will be the person that engineers and design owners come to for the deployment verdict. Your work will have global impact across multiple organizational goals and program-related metrics.

- You'll operate with complete independence in an area where business and infrastructure build strategy may not yet be defined.
- You will spend real time on the floor, next to the machines and the teams installing them, which is exactly where this role earns its credibility and its impact.
- You'll partner with other Robotics teams to validate design improvements and quantify realized savings against targets.
- You'll drive the cultural shift across the organization: coaching teams to stop absorbing complexity and start preventing it, building confidence in deployment engineers to challenge design decisions with data, and establishing new norms where field intelligence flows systematically back to product teams.

No two days will be the same in our fast-paced environment, offering opportunities for strategic impact as part of a collaborative, high-performing team.

About the team
Robotics Delivery & Packaging Innovation is a diverse and multi-talented team with a proven track record of overcoming challenging technical problems to deliver Amazon’s leading-edge robotics technologies in its fulfillment, transportation, and delivery network across the world. Our high-performing team blends engineering know-how, problem solving, curiosity, innovation, leadership, and effective communication to deliver positive results for our customers.

Come join our EU International Technology (EU INTech) team! We are seeking a customer-focused, analytically and technically skilled Sr. Technical Program Manager to innovate on behalf of customers, build effective solutions and deliver initiatives for Selection Availability & Intelligence (SAI).

SAI answers a fundamental question for every item in our catalog: should Amazon carry it, surface it, and grow it? This is a strategic and complex challenges, spanning substitution science, delivery speed perception, cross-border fulfillment, and intelligent selection curation.

Within SAI, the Serra team owns two programs: Zephyr (Substitution) — which identifies nearly identical products that ship faster, arrive sooner, and cost less to fulfill — and Smart Speed, which closes the gap between operational delivery improvements and customer perception of Prime speed. Both programs operate entirely through away-team coordination, requiring alignment across SCOT, PDEX, Cart, Search, BuyX, and international marketplace teams.

The XFN (Cross-Fulfillment Network) team curates and shares domestic and cross-border selection across EU and NA stores. XFN is shifting from simply enabling all selection to intelligently deciding what selection deserves to be assorted — balancing profitability, customer demand, and cost-to-serve through AI-powered tools and selection intelligence frameworks.

We have a roadmap focused on accelerating Serra's experiment velocity across OneDelivery and Delivery Speed CX, while supporting XFN's transformation into an intelligent selection platform. This TPM will own all Serra program delivery end-to-end and support a subset of XFN's highest-priority initiatives, coordinating across science, engineering, and product teams to ship at pace.

Key job responsibilities
- Translate business and technical requirements into actionable roadmaps by partnering with stakeholders across business and tech teams.
- Influence the direction of engineering teams within the organization by collaborating closely with customers in Tech and Business.
- Establish mechanisms that promote agility and engineering excellence through continuous iterations to achieve optimal outcomes.
- Manage program-level schedules and milestones, maintain alignment with multiple competing goals by negotiating and exhibiting influence over authority.
- Own the resource planning, execution, and delivery of projects on the roadmap.
- Assess and manage risks, define and measure success metrics, anticipate and resolve bottlenecks, provide escalation management, make tradeoffs, and balance customer needs with technical constraints.
- Proactively identify and resolve strategic issues that may impair the team's ability to meet business goals.
- Synthesize problems and solutions into a simple and consumable manner, and communicate effectively to a cross-functional audience as a subject matter expert.
- Regularly present work accomplished, challenges faced by teams, and recommend mitigation strategies to senior leadership.

Customer Fulfilment, or CF, is where it all started for Amazon. CF has scaled up from a humble team of booksellers to a sophisticated global team which handles more than 1.5 million orders every day. With the help of emerging technology, we’re always looking for ways to offer a bigger, better product range – delivered quickly and affordably.

Our centres are sometimes referred to as the ‘First Mile’ because it’s where most Amazon packages start their journey. We help to manage dynamic inventory and facilitate speedy deliveries round the clock.

Lots of different people work in our Fulfilment Centres, so there are plenty of opportunities for every skillset. Some of us work with physical products, while others analyse data to help everyone across the business make smart decisions.
