target_jobs.description:
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we're the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we're looking for talented people who want to help.
You'll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You'll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you'll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.
About the Role
The AWS Non-Standard Infrastructure Global Delivery Team builds and scales infrastructure for AWS programs that don't fit neatly into traditional data center models. Our projects are tailored to the specific needs of internal and external customers — from satellite ground stations that downlink data from orbit, to specialized labs where engineers develop custom silicon and push the boundaries of quantum computing, to purpose-built environments with precision environmental controls for archival storage systems, to infrastructure that extends the AWS network to the furthest edge of its global footprint. Each program brings its own constraints, its own technical requirements, and often its own first-of-kind design challenges.
What makes this team unique is the degree of ambiguity we operate in. Many of our projects begin as loosely defined requests from internal customer teams who know what they need to accomplish but not necessarily what infrastructure it takes to get there. A significant part of this role is working upstream with those customers to develop initial requirements, define technical scope, build demand forecasts, and refine scaling models — often for infrastructure types where no established playbook exists. The solutions we deliver are boutique by nature: custom-designed to meet specific programmatic needs, site constraints, and operational models that vary from project to project.
The scope is broad, the problems are novel, and the pace of growth means we are constantly onboarding new infrastructure types and scaling models.
If you thrive in ambiguity, enjoy the challenge of translating vague asks into engineered solutions, and want to shape how AWS builds and scales its infrastructure globally — this role is for you.
We have an immediate opening for a Technical Infrastructure Program Manager III to drive capacity delivery across multiple non-standard infrastructure programs worldwide. You will lead cross-functional teams through the full lifecycle of infrastructure delivery — from upstream requirements definition and demand forecasting through design development, procurement, construction, commissioning, and deployment. You will develop and implement scalable mechanisms for tracking program health, drive data-driven decisions influencing significant capital investments, and work with stakeholders across AWS to solve constraints, remove blockers, and accelerate delivery.
Your work will span:
- Requirements development — Working with internal customer teams to translate ambiguous needs into defined technical requirements, scope documents, and infrastructure specifications for novel deployment types
- Stakeholder management and influence — Navigating complex, matrixed organizational structures and influencing without authority to align diverse teams, secure resources, drive decisions, and maintain momentum across programs where no single team owns the end-to-end outcome
- Demand forecasting and capacity planning — Building initial demand models and scaling forecasts for programs where historical baselines don't exist, and refining them as programs mature
- Boutique design coordination — Partnering with engineering teams to develop tailored infrastructure solutions that meet unique programmatic constraints (environmental, regulatory, physical, operational)
- Multi-year delivery execution — Driving complex, globally distributed projects from conceptual feasibility through budget approval, design, procurement, construction, and commissioning
- Cross-program coordination — Identifying synergies, shared solutions, and lessons learned across a diverse portfolio of infrastructure types
- Mechanism development — Building scalable processes and reporting to monitor delivery health, drive accountability, and escalate to leadership as the portfolio grows
This role offers an opportunity to drive and influence business-critical decisions impacting the long-term future of AWS, working at the leading edge of emerging capability and service offerings. You must be comfortable managing remote project teams delivering novel — and sometimes pioneering — solutions across multiple countries and time zones; operating as the connective tissue between customer teams with undefined needs and engineering teams who build solutions; assessing and mitigating downstream risk; troubleshooting unforeseen implementation issues; removing barriers to project success; and operating effectively amid persistent uncertainty and change.
Up to 15% domestic and international travel may be necessary to support AWS non-standard infrastructure planning and scaling efforts.


Key job responsibilities
- Work upstream with internal customer teams to elicit, define, and document technical requirements for infrastructure programs that are often undefined or loosely scoped at inception
- Develop initial demand forecasts and capacity scaling models for emerging programs; refine forecasts as programs mature and data becomes available
- Lead end-to-end delivery of boutique infrastructure projects from requirements definition through design, procurement, construction, commissioning, and deployment
- Manage project budgets, schedules, and resource plans for programs with diverse and evolving technical requirements and site conditions
- Partner with engineering teams to develop tailored infrastructure solutions — working within unique constraints that vary by program, site, and customer need
- Coordinate cross-program activities to gain cost and execution efficiencies; identify and drive shared solutions and reusable design patterns
- Build and maintain relationships with internal customers (service teams, lab teams, engineering organizations) to align infrastructure delivery with evolving demand
- Convene partners and stakeholders to architect end-to-end process flows, delineate roles and responsibilities, and establish governance frameworks — transforming ambiguity into operational clarity, eliminating friction, and driving repeatable efficiencies across maturing programs
- Identify and mitigate risks in environments with limited precedent; develop contingency plans for first-of-kind deployment scenarios
- Develop scalable mechanisms, standard operating procedures, and process improvements to support rapid portfolio growth and new program onboarding
- Create data visualization reports and KPIs illustrating program health; escalate issues with clear recommendations to executive leadership


A day in the life
No two days are the same. You might start the morning in a requirements-definition session with a lab team that has a new hardware validation need but no infrastructure spec — helping them articulate what they actually need built. Then you shift to reviewing a demand forecast for a program expanding into new geographies, working with limited data and a lot of assumptions to refine. After lunch you're troubleshooting a procurement constraint on a boutique design that doesn't fit standard ordering mechanisms, followed by a cross-functional review of site conditions for a deployment in a venue that's never hosted this type of infrastructure before. You'll also spend time convening partners and stakeholders to architect process flows, delineate roles and responsibilities, and establish governance frameworks — transforming ambiguity into operational clarity, eliminating friction, and driving repeatable efficiencies across maturing programs. You'll regularly work with finance to secure capital, partner with engineering to translate customer intent into buildable designs, and look downstream to identify risks before they become blockers. The variety is the appeal — and the ability to navigate ambiguity, define scope where none existed, and drive delivery across technically diverse programs is what makes this role unique.

About the team
The Non-Standard Infrastructure team exists because AWS's growth doesn't stop at the walls of traditional data centers. We deliver capacity for programs whose infrastructure needs are unique, evolving, and often undefined at the outset. Our work starts upstream — helping customer teams figure out what they need — and carries through to handing over operational infrastructure that meets exacting requirements we helped define. Our team members are builders and translators: people who can sit with a scientist, engineer, or service owner, understand what they're trying to achieve, and turn that into a deliverable infrastructure program. If you're energized by variety, comfortable building the plane while flying it, and motivated by the impact of enabling AWS's most innovative services — you'll fit right in.

Based in London, the TIPM will lead cross functional teams to drive the implementation and deployment of data center expansion projects to meet the demands of our rapidly growing business.

• Clearly communicate goals, roles, responsibilities, and desired outcomes to internal cross-functional and remote teams.
• Up to 25% travel is envisaged within EMEA.

At Amazon Robotics, we are a dynamic team of passionate problem-solvers applying state-of-the-art robotics and software to tackle real-world challenges. Every day, we push the boundaries of innovation to transform customer experiences worldwide. We don’t just build technology—we invent new possibilities. And with the right tools, resources, and support, you’ll have the opportunity to create, innovate, and have fun along the way.

This team is a global squad of talented engineers that work diligently to resolve technical issues and help maintain Amazon’s robotic services, applications, and platforms. We are looking for an experienced technical manager to help support and grow our operations in this region.

Your team is responsible for front line customer support; resolving trouble tickets, responding to inquiries, and escalating safety, reliability, and performance issues. Your team will also develop and improve standard operating procedures, performance metrics, and feedback mechanisms to enable your technical support team to continue to effectively scale.

As a manager, you will not only help mentor and develop your team who form the foundation of this team but also learn how Amazon leverages state-of-the-art robotics technology to enhance our facilities and better serve our customers. You will engage with a dynamic technical environment, navigate complex situations, and ensure that your team is always set up for success. target_jobs.description:
Want to get close to the business? This VAT Manager role sits at the heart of Amazon's Digital & Devices operation, advising on global expansions, cross-border digital services, and new business models. Based in London, you'll work directly with product and commercial teams — translating complex VAT questions into clear, actionable guidance.

Key job responsibilities
- You will join a team of VAT specialists covering Amazon's Digital and Devices portfolio, taking ownership of specific business lines within that portfolio. Our team supports some of Amazon's most recognised and fastest-growing businesses — including Prime Video, Amazon MGM Studios, Alexa, Kindle, Audible, Amazon Music, Twitch, Devices (Ring, Eero), Appstore, Digital Software and Games, Amazon Prime, and M&A — as well as Amazon Leo, launching low earth orbit satellite broadband service for unserved and underserved communities worldwide.
- In your business lines, you will be the go-to VAT advisor: partnering directly with business teams to understand their commercial objectives and translating these into clear, pragmatic tax solutions. Your work will span product and service expansions, business restructurings, ESS obligations for cross-border digital services, e-invoicing launches, and the full range of operational VAT questions that arise in a fast-moving environment.
- Beyond your own portfolio, you will contribute to wider VAT and indirect tax strategy, communicating effectively around what your businesses are planning and helping make sure the tax response across all disciplines is consistent and timely.

A day in the life
Your day will typically move between the technical and the commercial. You might start the morning working through the VAT treatment of a new digital service launching in a new market — reviewing place of supply rules, checking e-invoicing requirements, and turning your analysis into a clear recommendation the business can act on. By mid-morning you could be on a call with finance and legal colleagues, aligning on the indirect tax position for a content acquisition deal before contracts are signed.
Your stakeholders are the product, finance, legal, and operations teams behind the businesses you support. Your job is to understand what they are building, get ahead of the tax implications, and stay with them through to implementation.

About the team
We are a global team based across London, Luxembourg, Sao Paolo, Seattle, New York and Washington DC, supporting some of Amazon's most exciting and innovative business lines.
Our mission is to help Amazon's digital businesses launch, expand, and scale. That means partnering with the businesses we support, from advice through to implementation, and staying close as the business evolves.
The team operates with a high degree of trust and autonomy. You will own your portfolio, but never work in isolation - we collaborate closely across direct tax, transfer pricing, and compliance teams, and share knowledge openly when things get complex.

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is looking for a world class partner strategy leader to join the EMEA Partner Specialist team to lead the partner strategy for Data — the database, analytics, and data services that form the foundation of the AI stack. As an EMEA Partner Lead, Data Foundations for AI, you will have an exciting opportunity to deliver on our strategy to accelerate adoption of the AWS data layer within partners of all types. You will help them identify and create data use cases and capabilities across the value chain — from getting data onto AWS and modernising it onto purpose-built engines, to unifying it in an Iceberg-native lakehouse, governing it for AI, and consuming it through AI-powered analytics — developing and executing go-to-market and enablement plans that lead to a healthy business pipeline, joint customer wins and market success.
Where a customer’s data lives determines where their AI runs. In this role, you will work with partners to help them establish AWS databases and analytics as the persistence and intelligence layer for every AI and agentic workload, building growth-oriented and strategically focused offerings that deliver on these customer and market expectations. In this endeavor, you will collaborate with a number of AWS internal teams including partner managers, solution architects, sales, BD, marketing, and solution teams to position and deliver these capabilities internally and to customers. The AWS Partner organization will look to you as the expert on the data domain, partner types, use cases, and how to drive AWS market success through partners. You will also act as a mentor to regional Data and Analytics experts, bringing your substantial experience in coaching and guiding the team into delivering customer and partner success.

Focus Areas
The EMEA Data Foundations for AI Partner Lead will focus on the following actions to address the data partner needs in the EMEA territory:
1. Identify industry-specific and horizontal data use cases and solution offerings across the six pillars — database migration and modernisation, Iceberg-native lakehouse, vector and agent-memory workloads, data governance, and AI-powered analytics — in the EMEA region;
2. Actively engage with mature and emerging Data & Analytics partners whose offerings align to these use cases (e.g. lakehouse and analytics ISVs such as ClickHouse, Snowflake, Neo4j and SAS positioning AWS-native alternatives against Databricks Unity Catalog and Snowflake-mediated Iceberg);
3. Identify and recruit horizontal or niche data partners we need in the ecosystem;
4. Lead enablement of our partner ecosystem (ISVs, SIs and GSIs) on native AWS data offerings including Amazon Aurora and Aurora DSQL, Amazon DynamoDB, Amazon Redshift, Amazon S3 Tables / Iceberg REST, AWS Lake Formation, and AWS Glue, and drive attainment of the new AWS Data Competency (launching at Partner Equip London, Sep–Oct 2026);
5. Enablement of the ASP organization on AWS and technology-partner data services and solutions. Success will be measured by # net new “must win” partners building Data Foundations for AI practices, # partner practitioners enabled on Data in EMEA (via PDM/PSA or PDS), # partners solutions launched, # customer references / case studies , # thought leadership (tech content, public speaking), # AO + PO Launched $ARR.

Role could be based in other EMEA AWS offices.

Key job responsibilities
• Develop and lead the partner strategy and execution plan to grow the AWS-based Data partner community in EMEA
• Drive AWS Data Competency attainment — guiding DB SDP partners, existing Data & Analytics competency partners, and high-propensity AI-only partners through cross-skill validation
• Collaborate with AWS teams and with partners to bring data solutions to market to meet customer needs, with measurable ROI results
• Prioritise AWS engagement with partners who focus on the data domain, including leading startups, consulting companies, and established ISV technology vendors
• Build C-level relationships with our top data partners
• Work with cross-functional groups in AWS to deliver training, enablement and go-to-market programs that scale the partner business across the data domain


About the team
Diverse Experiences
Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job
description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or
includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Why AWS?
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered
cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500
companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is
why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home,
there’s nothing we can’t achieve.

Inclusive Team Culture
AWS values curiosity and connection. Our employee-led and company-sponsored affinity groups promote inclusion and
empower our people to take pride in what makes us unique. Our inclusion events foster stronger, more collaborative
teams. Our continual innovation is fueled by the bold ideas, fresh perspectives, and passionate voices our teams bring to
everything we do.

Mentorship and Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find
endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-
rounded professional.

The role demands someone who can operate with equal confidence in a payments audit environment as in a DMA or GDPR compliance assessment — applying domain-agnostic assurance methodology across both disciplines.

- Develop and maintain Risk Control Matrices (RCMs) that map regulatory requirements to specific controls, evidence requirements, and testing procedures

- Manage audit findings, remediation tracking, and formal closure — including preparation of management responses and corrective action plans

- Drive detailed analysis of regulatory requirements in collaboration with legal teams, performing scoping and applicability assessments to determine which services, entities, and systems fall within scope

excluded_business_jobs.description:
Come build the future of international shipping at Amazon! We're seeking an exceptional commercial leader to define and scale the business strategy for Amazon Shipping's Cross Border solution, enabling seamless international parcel delivery across our operating geographies. As the Business Leader for Cross Border Shipping, you'll initially own the commercial strategy—developing go-to-market positioning, pricing, and customer acquisition—and then transition to program enablement and scaling as the solution matures into a complete cross-border offering. Working alongside dedicated Product and Technology partners, you'll shape how businesses and consumers ship internationally by leveraging Amazon's unparalleled logistics network, technology, and global footprint. You'll collaborate with talented teams across Amazon to solve complex challenges spanning customs, compliance, multi-country operations, and last-mile delivery to create a world-class cross-border shipping experience. If you're passionate about building something transformative and making a lasting impact on global commerce, this role is for you.

Commercial Strategy & Market Development:
Own and drive the comprehensive commercial strategy for Amazon Shipping's Cross Border program across all operating geographies. Develop pricing models, customer segmentation frameworks, and go-to-market strategies that position Amazon Shipping as a competitive alternative to major integrators for international parcel delivery. Identify and prioritize lane opportunities based on volume potential, margin attractiveness, and strategic value. Build and execute partnership strategies with customs brokers, international carriers, and trade facilitators. Define compelling value propositions for different customer segments—from SMB e-commerce sellers to enterprise shippers—and partner with Sales teams to drive customer acquisition and volume growth.

Program Enablement & Scaling: Lead the transition from commercial strategy to full program ownership as the Cross Border solution scales. Design and implement the operational and business framework required to support international shipping at scale—including process design, business requirements, compliance workflows, and customs/trade management. Define the program roadmap from pilot to general availability, establishing clear milestones and success criteria at each stage. Drive cross-functional alignment to ensure operational readiness across sortation, linehaul, customs clearance, and last-mile delivery in destination countries. Partner with Product and Technology counterparts to translate business requirements into scalable solutions, removing barriers to growth and ensuring consistent customer experience across all supported lanes.

Product Development: Partner with Product and Technology teams to define and prioritize the Cross Border product roadmap. Serve as the business voice driving requirements for customs documentation automation, multi-country rate engines, end-to-end tracking, and duty/tax transparency. Identify opportunities to leverage Amazon's existing infrastructure and technology to accelerate cross-border capabilities. Provide commercial input to pilot programs that test key hypotheses and gather shipper feedback. Drive continuous iteration on the customer experience based on market signals and competitive intelligence.

Operational Excellence & Compliance: Drive performance across cross-border-specific metrics including customs clearance SLA, landed-cost accuracy, transit time consistency, and shipment visibility. Partner with Operations and Compliance teams to ensure adherence to international trade regulations, export controls, and country-specific import requirements. Lead initiatives to reduce customs exceptions and clearance delays through proactive data quality and documentation standards. Define and track key performance indicators that measure program health and identify areas for operational improvement across all active lanes.
Strategic Leadership & Stakeholder Management:
Serve as the central commercial leader for Amazon Shipping's Cross Border initiative across a group of critical stakeholders. Build and maintain strong partnerships with Operations, Sales, Product, Legal, Finance, and international counterparts. Drive regular business reviews with senior leadership, providing strategic recommendations and progress updates on commercial performance and scaling milestones. Coordinate with regional teams to ensure consistent program implementation across geographies while maintaining flexibility for market-specific requirements and regulatory environments.
